test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Cast the first stone.

options.text: To be the first to criticize someone or something
To be the first to give a comment on an Instagram post
To be the first to invent something
To be the first to invite someone

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **To be the first to criticize someone or something**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Cast the first stone"** means to be the first person to criticize or blame someone, often hypocritically. (किसी को आलोचना या दोष देने वाला पहला व्यक्ति होना) • **Example: **Those who cast the first stone should make sure they are innocent themselves. • This idiom is derived from biblical references, where it warns against judging others if you are not free of fault yourself. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **To be the first to criticize someone or something**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 2: To be the first to give a comment on an Instagram post** (इंस्टाग्राम पोस्ट पर टिप्पणी करने वाला पहला व्यक्ति होना) • **Example: **She always tries to be the first to comment on her friends’ posts, but this does not relate to the given idiom. • **Option 3: To be the first to invent something** (कुछ आविष्कार करने वाला पहला व्यक्ति होना) • **Example: **Thomas Edison was the first to invent the electric bulb, but this does not match the meaning of the idiom. • **Option 4: To be the first to invite someone** (किसी को आमंत्रित करने वाला पहला व्यक्ति होना) • **Example: **He was the first to invite us to his party, but this option is unrelated to the idiom. 1aa:Tbbf, The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. People's actions have consequences that will eventually return to them.**
